narrative:
The model determined that you have a 59% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is above the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the amount you requested, and your credit history. Your checking account status had the greatest impact and pushed the decision strongly toward denial. Having a negative balance (under 0 DM) is relatively uncommon among approved applicants—only 12.6% of them show this status—whereas most approved borrowers have either no checking account or a positive balance. This signaled higher risk to the model.

Your credit history was the next most important factor and also increased the likelihood of being seen as a bad risk. While the majority of approved applicants have an “existing credits paid” record, your history of “all paid at bank” is rare (only 2.9% of approved cases) and the model interpreted it as less favorable.

The loan amount you requested worked in your favor. At 2,746 DM it was below the average requested by approved applicants (3,020 DM), which slightly lowered your risk score. Unfortunately, this positive influence was not enough to overcome the negative effects of your account status and credit history.

You should focus on building a stronger checking account balance and maintaining a more typical repayment pattern over the next 12–18 months. Once those areas improve, reapply or explore smaller loan options that better match your current profile.
